title: rule-guard refused three correct commands because their TEXT contained path-shaped and flag-shaped strings

first_order.what_broke: rule-guard.py blocked the change that introduces this very process, three times running. First it reported that the change staged runtime state; nothing runtime was staged, and the phrase it matched was English prose in the commit message. Then it reported a hook bypass on a command whose pathspec was four source files. Then it blocked a command containing no version-control invocation at all, because the file being written was prose describing those commands.
first_order.receipt: Three PreToolUse refusals on 2026-08-18 against commands whose actual arguments were docs/INCIDENT_PROCESS.md, docs/incidents, scripts/incident.py and .github/workflows/weekly-estate-review.yml. Two file writes were lost with the refused calls, because a rejected call executes nothing, including the parts the guard had no objection to.

cause_chain: The guard scans the raw command string for patterns instead of parsing the invocation and testing only its arguments.

A command string mixes several languages at once: the arguments, the flags, and any free text carried in a message or a heredoc. A substring scan cannot tell them apart, so text ABOUT a forbidden thing reads identically to the forbidden thing.

The failure is silent in a second way: a refusal aborts the whole call, so unrelated file writes batched into it are lost. Batching is the estate's own cost rule, which means the two rules fight each other.

CLASS: a guard that pattern-matches an unparsed command string produces confident false refusals, and the cost lands on correct work. Same class as INC-2026-08-18-stale-remote-ref, where a guard asked the local cache a question about the remote.

second_order.note: NOT YET RUN. Every PreToolUse guard in ~/.claude/scripts receives the same raw command string, so the sibling count is likely to be most of them.

third_order.note: The fix is to parse the argv and test only the positional arguments, ignoring anything after a message flag or inside a heredoc. Not written yet. Note also that ~/.claude is not a version-controlled tree, so none of these guards are reviewed or tested, and a change to one cannot be graded. That is a separate incident waiting to be recorded.

grade.signature: a PreToolUse guard matching a pattern in an unparsed command string
